event.summary: A failed per-place status read removes container rebuild controls without recovery
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 350a4b33b6d4476f4a78e43cea124bc2b828f462. TLDR: if a container build-status request fails once, Settings replaces the status and Rebuild controls with an error and provides no way to retry there. On an idle, healthy fleet connection it can remain that way until an unrelated change or reopening Settings. Details: recipes.rs:378-385 creates a use_resource that calls fetch_recipe_places and restarts only when observed_places changes or a fleet notice arrives. containers_settings.rs:209-218 renders Err as only an alert; the per-place Rebuild controls exist only in the Ok branch (257-285). No prior successful rows survive Err. The visible Retry loading control at recipes.rs:540-545 only invokes reload, whose implementation at 401-417 calls fetch_recipes, not place_status. RecipePlaces' on_refresh is reachable only after a successful Rebuild (containers_settings.rs:278). Source checks settled the missing premise: feed.rs:280-283 explicitly says notifications are spent even if reads fail; 289-315 only reacts to notice count changes. environment_ui.rs:713-725 does not poll settled places while the feed is healthy, and EnvironmentPlaceView has only place/name/reason/refreshing (farhelm-proto/src/environment.rs:135-141), so even identical fallback cache reads cannot change the observed_places memo. Thus healthy idle SSE does not provide recovery or retries. Contract: SPEC.md recipe catalog paragraph, lines 477-479, says: 'A list refresh that fails keeps the rows shown, says they may be out of date, and offers **Retry loading**.' Suggested fix: make per-place reads retain successful data and expose a working retry or use the shared surface reader's retry scheduling; ensure the catalog retry covers this resource. Suggested bucket: high (temporary request failure removes the user's container build visibility and all its rebuild controls indefinitely in the open panel). Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route. Confidence: confirmed by source and contracts; not executed. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none. Caveats: reopening Settings, a new fleet notice, or an actually changed place observation recovers; this is not a claim of backend build failure or resource loss.

The catalog Retry loading at recipes.rs:540-545 is conditional on the separate recipe read_error and calls only reload/fetch_recipes at 401-417. It may therefore be absent when only per-place status fails, and does not retry this request even when present. No retry follows Err itself. api/environments.rs:29-38, api.rs:2416-2443,2482-2548 confirm a single bounded execution and returned error, not a request-level retry ladder. UI lifecycle: RecipeList hooks run before its editor/list return at recipes.rs:448-462; opening and cancelling an editor leaves this resource alive. settings.rs:312-314,629-647 keeps Recipes mounted under hidden sections, so switching sections and back does not restart it. This qualifies the earlier wording: ordinary user actions can recover it, but they are mutation workarounds rather than a retry for the displayed error. Containers Refresh check: containers_settings.rs:17,53-63 owns a separate use_environment_places hook and invokes only that hook's refresh plus container-leftover reload. event.summary: Recipe list clones the complete status matrix for every row
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 350a4b33b6d4476f4a78e43cea124bc2b828f462. Discovery pass 2. TLDR: as the shared recipe catalog grows, rendering it repeatedly copies every recipe's build status into every row, even though each row displays only its own statuses. This adds quadratic allocation/copying work to opening and refreshing Settings. Details: recipes.rs:478-485 iterates N recipes and evaluates place_status.read().as_ref().cloned() for each RecipePlaces component. The resource value is Option<Result<Vec<RecipePlaceView>,String>>, and RecipePlaceView derives ordinary Clone over owned recipe/reason/step Strings (farhelm-proto/src/environment.rs:118-130). This is a deep Vec/String clone per row, not an Arc/Rc view. RecipePlaces takes that owned full Vec at containers_settings.rs:192-207 and only afterward filters all entries by row.recipe and container_host at 216-218; entries belonging to all other recipes were already copied. The endpoint at helm hosts.rs:4347-4368 returns one global vector containing each recipe's recorded/supported places. With N recipes each supporting P available places, the per-row clone evaluates N times on an N*P-element matrix, yielding O(N^2*P) copied status entries plus per-child filtering when those children render. This cost occurs before any framework child-prop equality optimization could avoid child rendering. Bounds checked: tensorlake/build.rs:235-264 selects every stored recipe without LIMIT; recipe create at tensorlake/recipes.rs:251-280 admits valid unique names without a catalog-count cap. The 64-KiB request-body cap is per recipe, not a list-size limit. API fetch_recipes at ui api/tensorlake_recipes.rs:47-57 returns all entries; there is no UI paging before the loop. RecipeList also subscribes to ACTIVITY_NOW at recipes.rs:364; activity.rs:75,99-110 republishes it every 30 seconds, so this allocation path can repeat in an idle open panel, in addition to ordinary read completions and feed-triggered renders. Useful checks establish this complexity without a benchmark; no particular freeze threshold, measured latency, OOM or crash is claimed. Contract/context: SPEC.md:441-479 requires one shared catalog with per-place build status, and SPEC_impl.md:6513-6516 specifies synchronous shared-state projection; neither requires each row to own every other recipe's status. Suggested fix: index statuses once by recipe and pass only the corresponding row's statuses, or share one immutable response without per-row deep cloning; retain the independent per-place request/retry semantics. Suggested bucket: other for an established avoidable resource-growth/performance defect, with material user-visible severity unmeasured and no parent priority accepted. Could-be-highest: no established security or user-work-loss route. Confidence: confirmed source-level allocation/complexity route, not runtime-observed performance. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none in the current supplied neighbour projection; no prohibited coverage sources searched. Caveats: small catalogs may have negligible practical cost; P counts actual returned places, and no cost is asserted for an absent/unloaded status response.
